about: MUTATING — trigger ONE cluster converge NOW by starting the existing cluster-deploy-runner oneshot: the same unit the 10-minute timer runs (same User=david, same $HOME/env, same maintenance-wrap, same build+push+roll). The event-driven fast path — a dispatcher rule spawns this on a pr-train's merged-step-done, so the cluster converges ~1 minute after merge instead of waiting up to 10 minutes for the timer tick. It only ACCELERATES: cluster-deploy-runner.timer and cluster-watchdog remain the independent floor (they owe nothing to NATS/SoR, which this fast path does — so a cluster-down event path costs latency, never a missed converge). Idempotent and self-guarding by construction of the script it starts: exits 0 if forge main has not moved vs the stamp, honors the converge hold file and the bricked-boot quarantine, so a redundant fire is a safe no-op. Runs infra/forge/converge-now.sh: `systemctl start --no-block` returns the moment systemd accepts the job (so the ~1-minute ops-runner never blocks on the build) — which is why this packet read `answered` on 2026-09-07 22:01 while the run it started died on a git lock (backlog d66f92b2). converge-now notes this packet's id (OPS_REQUEST_ID, from the runner's environment) in the checkout's inbox, and cluster-deploy-runner PATCHes this packet's metadata when the run ends: `converged: <sha>`, `converge_held: <reason>`, or `converge_failed: <stage> (exit N)`. THE READ-BACK (backlog 1058e686, car D): an accepted start is not a started run, so the script reads the unit's InvocationID/ActiveState/Result before the start and after it, and prints its effect line only for a NEW invocation that is activating or active (or already finished with Result=success); the same invocation as before is a converge already running that took the start into itself — exit 75, not yet, the note waits for the next run — a new invocation already failed is exit 1, and a unit that cannot be read is CANNOT ANSWER, exit 1, after the start, which runs regardless. Its own timeout, 60 s: the read-back waits up to 20 s of wall-clock time (bash's $SECONDS, not a count of polls, so a slow systemctl cannot stretch it) for the new invocation, plus one read before the start and one after the bound. Authorized by David 2026-09-07 — same explicit per-verb process as reclaim-disk / rollback-to (this entry is a precedent for the PROCESS, not a loosened default).
effect: ^converge-now: started cluster-deploy-runner[.]service — read back: invocation [0-9a-f]{32} [(](activating|active|inactive, already finished: Result=success)[)], was
